text.p: Italian bond futures held to easier levels in late afternoon trading but were off the day's lows supported by the rebound in German bunds which moved back into positive territory, dealers said.

However, the Italian market was still in an uncertain mood after the Bonn government appeared to have back down in its battle over the revaluation of gold assets, and awaiting any developments on the start of the single European currency.
"We are looking abroad for news with attention fixed on Germany and France. There was little on the domestic front to interest the market," said one LIFFE dealer.

Dealers said that the Italian market was still digesting the Socialist party election victory in France at the weekend and was concerned that this may lead to a delay in the start date for EMU or a watering down in its criteria.
The June LIFFE contract expired around midday today with the September contract down 45 basis points at 130.45 in late trade.
Italian official May CPI inflation released today showed a annual rise of 1.6 percent against April's 1.7 percent rise. The figure was generally in line with market expectations.
